classes.name: Hepatitis C direct-acting antivirals
classes.description: Sofosbuvir/velpatasvir (Epclusa and authorized generic), glecaprevir/pibrentasvir (Mavyret), ledipasvir/sofosbuvir (Harvoni and authorized generic), sofosbuvir/velpatasvir/voxilaprevir (Vosevi), elbasvir/grazoprevir (Zepatier).
classes.plainDescription: An 8 to 12 week course of pills that cures hepatitis C.

preferredAgent.sig: No cirrhosis or compensated cirrhosis: 1 tablet once daily for 12 weeks. Decompensated cirrhosis (Child-Pugh B or C): 1 tablet once daily plus weight-based ribavirin for 12 weeks (label).
preferredAgent.sigShort: 1 tab QD x12 wk (+ribavirin if decompensated)
preferredAgent.plainSig: One pill a day for 12 weeks; people with advanced liver scarring also take ribavirin.

records.preferredRestriction: PA required: simplified criteria (chronic HCV, treatment-naive, non-cirrhotic, uncomplicated; recent HCV RNA within 3 months; not pregnant) or non-simplified DAA class criteria; approval duration 16 weeks (PA criteria pp. 156-158).

paRequired.reason: Preferred with PA: PA required under the simplified or non-simplified DAA criteria (PA criteria pp. 156-158; PDL p. 4).
criteria: Simplified path: chronic HCV; Mavyret for 12 weeks; treatment-naive, non-cirrhotic (FIB-4 below 3.25), not pregnant, HIV-negative, HBsAg-negative, no liver transplant or HCC; HCV RNA within 3 months.

Standard path: acute or chronic HCV; regimen per label or guidelines; GI, hepatology, ID, or transplant prescriber; HCV RNA, genotype, HIV and HBsAg documented; prior DAA: retreatment and adherence answers.

paRequired.drug: Epclusa (sofosbuvir/velpatasvir) brand tablet and pellet pack
paRequired.reason: Not preferred: PA required. Approval needs clinical justification why Mavyret or generic sofosbuvir/velpatasvir cannot be used, plus DAA class criteria (PA criteria p. 158; PDL p. 4).
criteria: Clinical justification (allergy, contraindication, drug interaction, or intolerance) why Mavyret or sofosbuvir/velpatasvir cannot be used or is not indicated.
Meets the standard HCV criteria: acute or chronic HCV; regimen per label or guidelines; specialist prescriber; HCV RNA within 3 months, genotype, HIV and HBsAg status; Child-Pugh score if cirrhotic.

records.verificationNote: Read PDL p. 4 and PA criteria pp. 156-158. Generic sofosbuvir/velpatasvir is the Preferred-with-PA product, the lowest-barrier generic DAA. Standard label is 12 weeks; the PA approval window stated in the criteria is 16 weeks, so both are reported. Epclusa brand and Harvoni brand/generic are Non-preferred (PA), so the plan prefers the generic over the brand here; boglActive not set (generic is not the disfavored product). Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir generic is Non-preferred.
